test_title: PYST 49: SSC GD Constable - Quantitative Aptitude (Held on: 6th November 2021 Shift 3)
subject: maths
question: The total surface area of a solid cube is 294 cm². It is melted and recast into a right circular cylinder of radius 7 cm. What is the height (in cm, correct to one decimal place) of the cylinder? (Take π = frac{{22}}{7})
solution:
Concept:

The cylinder is to be cast from the solid cube. Hence, the volume of the cube would be equal to the volume of the re-cast cylinder.

Formula:

Volume of cylinder = π × r2 × h

TSA of cube = 6a2

Volume of cube = a3 

where-

r = radius of cylinder

h = height of cylinder

a = side of the cube

Calculation:

According to the question-

⇒ 6a2 = 294

⇒ a2 = 49 or a = 7 cm

Volume of solid cube = 7 × 7 × 7 = 343 cm3

Since Volume of solid cube = Volume of cylinder

⇒ 343 = 22over7 × 7 × 7 × h

⇒ h = 49over22 cm or 2.22 cm

∴ The height of the cylinder is 2.2 cm.
